verdict.root_cause: At 10:16:56 platform-automation updated ad's image reference to an ad-specific hotfix tag [tr_d0001383944f]; one second earlier ad wrote a clean, orderly gRPC-then-JVM shutdown and then emitted nothing at all for the rest of the window, with no startup lines [tr_7ce8853c40b5]. Ad produced zero server spans after 10:13:36 while pre-cutoff traces show healthy 1.6-10ms frontend→ad chains [tr_6b93e795e969]. Frontend's errors are purely transport-level gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE against a single peer 172.18.0.19:9555, refused and later host-unreachable, with no connection ever established [tr_3384ab529d86]. The replacement artifact never came up, so ad's address has nothing listening; frontend has no changes of its own [tr_877e05badcaa] and its raised error ratio [tr_ea08242c3d89] is the downstream shadow.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent ad-side signals converge on the same second: the image change at 10:16:56 [tr_d0001383944f], the orderly shutdown at 10:16:55 with silence after [tr_7ce8853c40b5], and the hard cutoff of ad spans with no post-cutoff inbound server span of any kind [tr_6b93e795e969]. The caller's signature discriminates the look-alikes: ECONNREFUSED with no connection established is not a hang (freeze/partition) and not DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (dependency_latency), and slow-downstream plus DNS were both closed explicitly [tr_3384ab529d86]. The clean sequenced shutdown with no stack trace rules out an OOM kill, and the last memory-limit action before onset was a restore at 10:03 [tr_d0001383944f][tr_7ce8853c40b5]. Ad's own error ratio never departed baseline or approached saturation [tr_e5e86ff39423], consistent with a service that stopped serving rather than one serving badly. What is wrong now is that the artifact that should answer on ad's address is not running; the fix is restoring the prior image.
open_questions: The 172.18.0.19:9555 → ad mapping is inferred from port and timing; frontend logs name only IP:port and no registry or inventory was consulted [tr_3384ab529d86].

Frontend was already logging identical UNAVAILABLE errors against that peer at 09:54, while ad was demonstrably serving traces at 10:06-10:13 [tr_3384ab529d86][tr_6b93e795e969] — unexplained, and it weakens the 10:16:56 onset story.
Why the new artifact failed to start is unknown (pull failure, crash before logging, never scheduled are indistinguishable), and no CPU/memory metrics for ad were ever collected [tr_e5e86ff39423].

alternatives.root_cause: Repeated lowering of ad's memory limit by platform-automation caused the JVM to be killed, leaving ad absent; the hotfix image is incidental.
alternatives.why_not: No lowered limit was in force at onset (restored at 10:03) and the termination was an orderly shutdown with no stack trace [tr_d0001383944f][tr_7ce8853c40b5]; it survives only because no utilisation metrics were gathered and it could explain the 09:54 refusals.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad container was stopped and removed by the orchestrator independently of the artifact change, so ad is simply absent rather than running a bad build.
alternatives.why_not: The shutdown coincides within one second of a recorded image update, which is the obvious proximate act [tr_d0001383944f]; this reading requires that coincidence to be accidental, though the refused→host-unreachable shift at ~10:23:47 [tr_3384ab529d86] keeps it alive.
